items.title: Fast & Furious TV Show Greenlit at Peacock, With Vin Diesel as Executive Producer
items.excerpt: The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.
items.content_text: The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer. As reported by Deadline on October 1, 2026, Peacock has officially given the green light for a Fast & Furious show. The series is slated to premier in 2028, the same year that the very last movie in the franchise is also set to release. Vin Diesel first mentioned the show in May 2026 during a talk at NBCUniversal’s Upfront event, where he explained that fan demand drove Universal Pictures to consider expanding its high-octane IP. “As you all know, we are very precious about these movies but over the last decade, we’ve realized that the fans have wanted more, they wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories,” he said at the event. “And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space.” Oh and of course, family was part of that decision: “That’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family will be protected in the TV space,” he added. Mike Daniels (Sons of Anarchy, PONIES) and Wolfe Coleman (9-1-1: Lone Star) are both writers and co-runners for the show, which is one of four series planned for the Fast & Furious universe. As told by Deadline, one of these shows will be helmed by Nick Wooton (The Endgame) and Charmaine DeGraté (House of the Dragon), while the other two will be handled by Joe Henderson (Lucifer) and Ingrid Escajeda (Griselda). With this in mind, it doesn’t look like the Fast & Furious world is set to end anytime soon, although its final film is on the horizon. This last movie, titled Fast Forever , is slated to release on March 17, 2028. It will mark the eleventh entry in the film franchise. Vin Diesel spoke about the movie at Fuel Fest in June, where he detailed how he negotiated with Universal Pictures to bring its last adventure back to Los Angeles. “The studio said to me, ‘Vin, can we please have the finale of Fast and Furious [in] April 2027?'” he told fans at the event. “I said, ‘Under three conditions.’ First, is to bring the franchise back to L.A.! The second thing was to return to the car culture, to the street racing! The third thing was reuniting Dom and Brian O’Conner.” Given that O’Conner was played by the late Paul Walker, this statement led fans to wonder how the character will return. Walker’s brother was firmly against the idea of portraying his sibling in in Fast Forever, suggesting that AI could be used to bring him back to the franchise, instead. Image Credits: Earl Gibson III/Deadline via Getty Images
items.title_en: Fast & Furious TV Show Greenlit at Peacock, With Vin Diesel as Executive Producer

items.title: Viral Short Horror Film Portrait of God Gets Feature Length Movie Starring Chase Infiniti
items.excerpt: Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.
items.content_text: Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video. If you’re an avid horror fan, chances are you’ve watched Dylan Clark’s viral horror short Portrait of God on YouTube at some point. The seven-and-a-half-minute video centers on college student Mia Reilly as she rehearses a presentation; her topic discusses a mysterious painting — or rather, a photograph of a painting — that, some say, shows a portrait of God. The photo of said portrait is simply a black image, but testimonies from viewers tell a different story. Reilly says that “some insist they see a person in the darkness,” with subjects claiming in audio recordings that they see a “wrinkled, skinny” man — or at least, something that’s “close to a man.” I won’t spoil the rest of the short for you, but I highly recommend checking it out if you haven’t seen it yet. Clark packed quite a punch in such a short amount of time, with his video racking up over 10 million views since being uploaded four years ago, and it seems like major studios took notice. As shared by The Hollywood Reporter , the film has been greenlit by Lionsgate Studios, with Sam Raimi for Ghost House Pictures and Jordan Peele for Monkeypaw set to produce. This is the first time these two have collaborated on a project together. They aren’t the first to get their hands on Clark’s IP, though; Portrait of God was previously snagged by Universal, but the project fell through in early 2026. Things seem substantially more stable now, given the producers attached, as well as a major actress set to star in the film: Chase Infiniti, who gained wide acclaim for her breakout role in One Battle After Another . “We’re delighted to deepen our creative partnership with Dylan Clark, whose remarkable talent and distinctive perspective make him one of the most exciting emerging voices in horror,” Lionsgate film’s Adam Fogelson said in a statement. “With Sam and Jordan, two of the genre’s most influential producers, the extraordinary Chase Infiniti starring, and Dylan at the helm, this is an exceptional creative team. We believe they have all the ingredients for a film that is haunting, thought-provoking, and scary as hell.” “With Blair Witch, I’m experiencing firsthand the trust Lionsgate places in its filmmakers, and I couldn’t be happier that Portrait of God has found a home there, as well,” Clark added. “I’m also thrilled to welcome Chase Infiniti to our team. She blew me away in One Battle After Another and is one of the most exciting young actors working today.” It’s a big time for indie horror flicks, especially where YouTubers are concerned; Kane Parsons’ Backrooms and Curry Barker’s Obsession were smash hits at the box office, opening the way for adaptations of other popular internet creepypastas like Siren Head (to be produced by Zach Cregger), The Mandela Catalogue , and even The SCP Foundation. Image Credits: Monica Schipper/Getty Images
items.title_en: Viral Short Horror Film Portrait of God Gets Feature Length Movie Starring Chase Infiniti

items.title: Lanterns Rakes In More Than 18 Million Views Per Episode Globally As Season Finale Approaches
items.excerpt: It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt.
items.content_text: It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt. As shared by Variety , statistics compiled by media research firm Nielsen show that Lanterns’ seventh episode accrued seven million views within the United States during its first three days, combined across HBO’s cable channels and its streaming service, HBO Max. In the US, Lanterns is reportedly averaging more than 12 million views per episode; that number increases to 19 million when taking global viewership into account. Variety notes that it’s highly likely these numbers will continue to rise, as 1.5 million new viewers reportedly watched Lanterns’ premier episode just last week. This is good news for fans of the newly-rebooted DCU, but it’s not surprising; Lanterns has been a big hit with audiences and critics alike, though it’s caused no end of debate among hardcore Lanterns fans, given the fate of one of its central characters. (There’s still hope that this particular person might still be around, though, thanks to some convincing theories making the rounds online.) With these latest stats in mind, Lanterns is rubbing elbows with other uber-popular HBO releases; DC’s previous series on the streamer, The Penguin , averaged 27 million views per episode back in 2024, while shows like Euphoria averaged 25 million per episode by the end of its third and final season. Award-winning medical drama The Pitt averaged 15.4 million views on Season 2, the finale of which garnered 9.7 million views. Lanterns is gearing up for its season finale, which airs on HBO Max this coming Sunday, October 4. We have a few burning questions that still need to be answered, and its latest episode has fueled oodles of fan theories, not to mention memes (mostly about Mogo and John Stewart). IGN’s Jesse Schedeen scored its latest episode an eight out of 10 , praising it for regaining the series lost momentum from episode seven and reconnecting with the “core Hal/John dynamic we love so much."

items.title: New GTA 6 Age Rating Confirms Game Will Feature Sex Scenes
items.excerpt: GTA 6 will have sex scenes, according to a new listing from international ratings boards.
items.content_text: GTA 6 will have sex scenes, according to a new listing from international ratings boards. In New Zealand and Australia, GTA 6's store page on PlayStation was updated to include the game's official age rating. A similar thing happened this morning with the UK and American versions of the game , but the New Zealand and Australia versions offer one distinct difference: the mention of sex scenes. Yes, it's true: there will be intercourse in GTA 6. If you're asking yourself, "Is that different from GTA 5?" Yes, it appears to be. GTA 5's rating makes no mention of sex scenes, despite there being at least one. Midway through the game, Trevor can be seen getting freaky with Johnny Klebitz's girlfriend (granted, it's pretty brief). GTA 6's sex scenes may be much more detailed and graphic, especially since the story revolves around the romantic relationship between Jason and Lucia. Various trailers have shown sensual, intimate scenes between the two characters, so it's possible that the full game will feature some pretty spicy material. Ultimately, it looks like Rockstar isn't pulling any punches with GTA 6. Rating descriptions have mentioned blood and gore, intense violence, drug use, and more, so it looks like we're in for yet another edgy GTA game. The developer has managed to keep a lot under wraps, but recently revealed that it visited strip clubs in Florida for "research purposes." We're officially just a month away from GTA 6's release date, so there are sure to be many more marketing beats in the coming weeks. Whether that brings a new trailer or other forms of marketing remains to be seen, but Rockstar has shelled out serious dough for an ad on top of the Miami Heat's arena in Florida and has begun placing ads in New York as of today.
items.title_en: New GTA 6 Age Rating Confirms Game Will Feature Sex Scenes

items.title: Miami Vice '85 Casts Walton Goggins in Villain Role
items.excerpt: Walton Goggins has joined the cast of Miami Vice '85. The actor will play a henchman/assassin acting on behalf of John Leguizamo's character, who is a cartel king and the lead villain in the film.
items.content_text: Walton Goggins will play a villain in Miami Vice '85 . Deadline reports that Goggins, who has made a name for himself in recent years via Fallout and The White Lotus, will leverage his nefarious qualities on the big screen in 2028. The actor will play a henchman/assassin acting on behalf of John Leguizamo's character , who is a cartel king and the lead villain in the film. The two villains will be contending with characters played by Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler, who will play Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively. Not much is known about the film right now, but it is expected to be a period reboot of the iconic TV series. It's not a sequel to Michael Mann's own film adaptation of the TV series or an extension of the original source material. The film will be helmed by F1 and Top Gun: Maverick director Joseph Kosinski. The project was initially slated for a 2027 release, but was pushed back to May 2028 . It is expected to begin filming sometime this year, so expect more casting announcements in the coming weeks as production ramps up. Walton Goggins has made a name for himself by playing treacherous characters. He made the rounds as a variety of shady TV characters on shows like Justified, The Shield, and more. He has also starred in films like The Hateful Eight, Ant-Man and the Wasp, and Tomb Raider. He's arguably best known these days for playing The Ghoul, a sort of anti-hero in Fallout that has been corrupted by the Wasteland while searching for his long-lost family. items.title: Amazon Launches New Line of Kindles and Accessories Right Before Prime Big Deal Days
items.content_text: Amazon has revealed its 2026 line of Kindle devices just a few days before its Prime Big Deal Days sale. The refresh includes a brand new Kindle, Kindle Paperwhite, and Kindle Colorsoft, along with new accessories and Kids Editions of these tablets. All of the new devices and accessories are now available to buy or preorder on Amazon, and you can check out the official press release for specifics on each device. With the release of new models, older Kindle devices are getting discounted as part of Amazon's sale as well. New Kindle Device Pricing and Details Amazon releases new Kindle devices pretty much every year, and in the past, the improvements were incremental. The biggest changes to the 2026 models include Amazon making them thinner, lighter, and faster than previous iterations of the e-readers. It also introduced aluminum hardware options and other highly requested features like cover page turning for their new Signature Editions of the Paperwhite and Colorsoft models. According to Amazon's press release, the new standard Kindle will be 30% faster when opening books and will have edge-to-edge color across the full lineup. The Kindle is still arguably the best reading tablet on the market. With Amazon removing support for older device models earlier this year, it's worth considering an upgrade to a newer version. It's important to note that all Kindle devices released after 2024 will include most of the latest features and will be compatible with newer accessories via Bluetooth. The Kindle Click Is the Best New Accessory A Kindle is already pretty convenient, but what if it could be even more convenient? Amazon has announced a remote that will turn the pages for you. Third-party Kindle page-turners have been available for years now, but this is the first time Amazon has made a Bluetooth-compatible version that doesn't actually need to physically touch the screen to get the page to turn. At $34.99, the new Amazon Kindle Click will work with any Kindle model released in 2024 or later. It's currently set to release on October 28 alongside most of the new 2026 Kindles. In addition to the remote, Amazon is also releasing new Kindle covers that include physical page-turning buttons. Both of these new accessories are bringing back a physical experience to an otherwise digital product.
items.title_en: Amazon Launches New Line of Kindles and Accessories Right Before Prime Big Deal Days

items.title: Danny McBride's G.I. Joe Movie Casts Bradley Cooper as Duke
items.excerpt: Bradley Cooper will star as Duke in the upcoming G.I. Joe movie, directed by Danny McBride.
items.content_text: Bradley Cooper will star as Duke in the upcoming G.I. Joe movie, directed by Danny McBride. McBride has been developing a new G.I. Joe movie for Paramount for some time, and it appears to be gaining some steam. After months of rumors, Deadline reports that Bradley Cooper will star as Duke, the leader of the titular group. McBride has reportedly had Cooper at the top of his wishlist for the film's cast, but there were questions over whether or not it was feasible. Cooper is currently starring in and directing an Ocean's 11 prequel in Europe, so he's got his hands full. However, Deadline claims that Cooper liked the script so much that he signed on and committed to the film. As of right now, it's unclear when the film will shoot, but presumably it won't be sometime until next summer at the earliest. Cooper's Ocean's prequel is slated to hit theaters in June 2027, and he will likely oversee post-production and go on an extensive press tour, which would likely prevent him from leading an action-heavy film until he fulfills his prior obligations. Nevertheless, it's a big win and solid star power for McBride's film. Details are scarce, but McBride has stated that the film will take place in Springfield , a town that is secretly populated by members of Cobra. He also confirmed that the film will be a suspenseful action movie, rather than a comedy, which is where McBride's roots mainly lie. He has proven himself capable outside of comedy, however. McBride co-wrote the recent trilogy of Halloween films, and while divisive by the end of their run, those movies showed McBride doesn't lean on unnecessary humor to get through a script. McBride will co-write the G.I. Joe film with Jeff Fradley and John Carcieri. As of right now, we're not sure who else will end up in the film's cast, but if Cooper is leading, it certainly shows that there's a level of prestige backing the project. The last attempt at a series of G.I. Joe films featured the likes of Channing Tatum and The Rock, but were critically panned. Cooper has elevated himself to a higher caliber in recent years after directing and starring in Oscar-nominated films like A Star Is Born , so it'll be interesting to see who else he gets paired with. Photo by Samir Hussein/WireImage
items.title_en: Danny McBride's G.I. Joe Movie Casts Bradley Cooper as Duke

items.title: New Pokémon x ESA Collection Includes the Astronaut Pikachu Plush That Went to Space
items.content_text: Pokémon's collaboration with the European Space Agency has officially led to a merch drop. The new collection includes two new Pikachu plushies, listed at $29.99, which feature the electric-type Pokemon in two versions of the ESA space suit. Recognize the design? The new plush is modelled after the Pikachu plush ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot took on her flight to the International Space Station earlier this year . The collection also includes apparel, pins, and plenty of TCG accessories, now available directly from The Pokémon Center . Pokemon x ESA Collection Drops Ahead of World Space Week The collaboration between Pokémon and ESA kicked off on April 11, when the original astronaut Pikachu plush was launched into space. The plush spent a grand total of 67 days in orbit at the International Space Station, circling Earth over 1,000 times. Now, the partnership is coming back to Earth. The Pokémon Center's new collection is dropping ahead of World Space Week, which kicks off on October 4. That date will also see the launch of a new space-themed event in Pokémon GO and interactive “Space and Pokémon” exhibitions in select museums across Europe. For those of us on the other side of the pond? Well, at least we get merch. The new TCG accessories, led by a binder, deck box, and playmat, all show illustrations of astronaut Pikachu floating alongside Lunatone, Cosmog, and Minior. Fans can also get their hands on T-shirts and hoodies with the same cosmic Pokémon graphic. The most expensive item in the drop is a full bomber jacket, listed at $129.99, which features individual Pokémon patches and a Poké Ball zipper. The Pokémon franchise is marking its 30th anniversary this year, and there have been plenty of partnerships to celebrate. Here’s TPC’s statement on the ethos behind this particular collaboration: “The European Space Agency (ESA) is Europe’s gateway to space. Its mission is to shape the development of Europe’s space capability and ensure that investment in space continues to deliver benefits to the citizens of Europe and the world. Together, ESA and Pokémon aim to inspire and delight with endless cosmic possibility!” While most of the collection is available for purchase now, one "delightful and inspiring" item that still doesn't have a release date is a new figure of Pikachu in his astronaut outfit. Just another thing for fans to look forward to during the long wait for Gen 10 .
items.title_en: New Pokémon x ESA Collection Includes the Astronaut Pikachu Plush That Went to Space

items.title: Riot Games Co-Founder Says 2XKO Needed ‘Hundreds of Thousands, if Not Millions’ of Monthly Active Players to Survive
items.excerpt: The co-founder, co-chairman, and chief product officer of Riot Games, Marc Merrill, revealed the number of monthly active users 2XKO would have needed to justify its budget, and the eye-popping amount has sparked an animated debate within the fighting game community.
items.content_text: The co-founder, co-chairman, and chief product officer of Riot Games, Marc Merrill, revealed the number of monthly active users 2XKO would have needed to justify its budget, and the eye-popping amount has sparked an animated debate within the fighting game community. Speaking on The Lemonade Stand , Merrill went into detail about what happened behind the scenes at Riot to cause 2XKO’s catastrophic failure, and provided a ballpark figure of monthly active users the game would have needed in order to justify how much money and time was spent on its development. It’s no surprise that this figure was, to put it lightly, pretty unrealistic for a fighting game; Merrill said that, considering its cost structure, 2XKO would have needed a player count “in the high hundreds of thousands, if not millions” to rationalize its continued support. Merrill also mentioned Street Fighter 6, saying the 2023 release of Capcom’s juggernaut title threw off their plans to take a big chunk of the fighting game community’s interest off the back of Street Fighter V. “I think we had a window to do some great things to really help the fighting game community, and then Street Fighter 6 came out, which was something like eight years after we started working on 2XKO,” Merrill explained. “We had an awesome development team of really talented people that did great work, that made a beautiful game. We’d already communicated all this stuff to players, and so we were like, ‘You know what? Let’s just keep going. Let’s give it to the community. Let’s see what happens, right?’ …I think if we came out, ideally when we should’ve, years before Street Fighter, I think we would have made a really significant impact on the community.” Merrill explained that Riot didn’t have internal “alignment” on the strategy for 2XKO, which caused “managerial fracturing” and confusion within the team. Ultimately, not enough players hopped on the game in order to justify the time and money spent on it, so Riot did what they thought was best — issued full refunds to players and canceled further content updates. “We’ve got nobody to blame but ourselves,” he said. “[2XKO] resonated with some players, but not nearly enough players in order to justify the sort of live service, long-tail approach that the game was designed to do. And so we were like, let’s just pivot, let’s create this box, give everybody a refund, say, ‘Hey, sorry we weren't able to achieve this incredibly high aspiration that we were trying to do for the fighting game community, but we love you guys, appreciate [you], hope they’ll play this game, like many other box games, for years to come, and here you go. Sorry we let you down,’ is sort of the orientation of what happened there.” For comparison, Street Fighter 6 — which is indisputably the biggest fighting game on the market right now — boasts an average of anywhere between 16,000 and 20,000 monthly active users on Steam (not including PlayStation, which doesn't share these statistics publicly). It’s understandable that Riot, the maker of massively popular MOBA League of Legends, might expect more than that — but even Riot themselves knew there was no way they could reach “millions” of monthly active users to justify keeping their tag fighter alive. Unsurprisingly, Merrill’s comments have sparked a swath of heated reactions within the fighting game community. Most players were left stunned that Riot felt such a high player count was necessary to keep 2XKO afloat, given how relatively "niche" the genre is. “It seems like they figured the game wasn't going to last long, but they spent so much money on it, so instead of immediately canning it, they released it to see if it would do anything,” one player mused . “Unfortunately, what it needed to do goes way beyond what any fighting game has ever done in existence lol.” “The way [Merrill said], ‘Then Street Fighter 6 came out,’ like that wasn't going to happen. SFV had one of the best comeback stories in fighting games. Did he really not think 6 was going to happen?” another asked . 2XKO was first revealed to the public as ‘Project L’ in 2019, though rumors of a fighting game based on the League of Legends IP had been swirling around long beforehand. Its confusing release (from a closed beta to extended early access) on the back of a lengthy development period essentially killed most of the hype around the game, and Riot officially announced plans to end active development after December 2026, though online play will still be supported.
items.title_en: Riot Games Co-Founder Says 2XKO Needed ‘Hundreds of Thousands, if Not Millions’ of Monthly Active Players to Survive

items.title: We Build LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants Bikini Bottom: a F.U.N. Build for Nostalgic Adults
items.excerpt: We build the SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom LEGO set, which offers a massive dose of nostalgia for millennial adults.
items.content_text: As a millenial, I grew up during what I consider the golden era of cartoons – the 1990's. Some of my favorites included Rugrats, The Angry Beavers, Hey Arnold!, and Rocko's Modern Life. But, just as the 90's came to a close, Nickelodeon dropped another certified classic on my young, impressionable mind. I knew there was something special about SpongeBob SquarePants from the very first episode, and now, more than 25 years later (wow, I feel old), it's one of the most popular children's cartoons of all time, and is still going strong with over 300 episodes. LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom (available now exclusively from the LEGO Store ) is the first new SpongeBob-themed set since 2012, and the first designed for adults with an 18+ age rating. It includes plenty of references and gags from the series, making it an excellent set for longtime fans to put together. Set: #11386 Ages: 18+ Pieces: 1,794 Dimensions: 10" (H) x 22" (W) x 6" (D) Price: $219.99 The original set featuring the iconic homes and denizens of Bikini Bottom released in 2006 , composed of just 579 pieces, and included a rather horrifying Squidward minifigure. Now, 20 years later, the set is much larger and has been completely reimagined for an older audience. At 1,794 pieces, more than three times the number of the original, this is also the largest LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants set released by far . The contents of the massive box are split across 14 bags. This is the second set I've built that uses LEGO's new eco-friendly packaging, which replaces the transparent polyethylene bags with paper bags, an initiative that began back in 2021 . While I appreciate the positive environmental impact these new bags promise, I've found that they are prone to having small pieces get stuck in the seams. If you're building a set that includes these new bags, be sure to double-check each one if you're potentially missing a piece. One aspect I really like about this set is just how good the minifigs look. Each one has been redesigned from the previous iterations, with more accurate colors and improved moldings. SpongeBob, in particular, looks great. The color is spot-on, and he finally has a proper pair of printed pants instead of looking like he's standing on a pair of brown stilts. SpongeBob also comes with his trusty jellyfish net. Patrick's minifig received a substantial redesign compared to his originals as his head and stomach are now one large piece that fit over the torso like a sort-of reverse cape that more accurately depicts his food-loving physique. He even comes with one of his favorite junk foods – a Neopolitan ice cream cone. Squidward got the biggest glow-up compared to his original minifig. Although later iterations fixed this by giving him a proper head mold, the version included in this set features a more accurate face, improved coloring, and little tentacles printed on the feet. While not minifigs per se, the set also comes with a buildable DoodleBob (complete with the Magic Pencil) and a buildable Gary the Snail, although it hasn't changed much from early LEGO iterations aside from having better coloring. He still doesn't have eyes, though. This set is divided into two instruction books, with the first book covering Patrick and Squidward's houses, and the second book dedicated entirely to SpongeBob's famous "Pineapple Under the Sea," which employs some unique tactics to get its shape – more on that later. There are also a number of smaller builds to round out the scenery, including the crooked Bikini Bottom sign, a Boatmobile, SpongeBob's Bubblestand, and small diorama of the Jellyfish Fields, with a small rotating platter to make the jellyfish swim around. Patrick's house doesn't take long to put together, as all of its contents fit in a single bag. After all, it is just a large rock covering a hole in the ground. Thankfully, LEGO didn't just stop there. The lid of Patrick's house can be opened to reveal all of his sand furniture, including his chair, lamp, rug, and CRT TV. It even includes a space for him to "sleep" under the lid. Squidward's house, split across six bags, is a little more involved to assemble as it's comprised of four floors: the bottom floor which features his clarinet and music sheet; the second floor with his canopy bed; and the third floor bathroom, complete with his toilet, shower, and bubble bath. There's also a shower curtain with what appears to be a silhouette of SpongeBob hiding behind it - a reference to the episode "Squid's Day Off," where Squidward becomes paranoid after leaving SpongeBob in charge of the Krusty Krab. Finally, the top floor of the house features Squidward's tanning bed that he frequently sets up in front of his house, along with a mirror and a flower-topped cocktail drink. The interior of the house repurposes some LEGO pieces in interesting ways, such as a pink-colored crown as a sea anemone plant and an upside down cupcake piece as the lampshades for Squidward's nightstands. LEGO absolutely nailed the exterior of Squidward's house. The dark blue pieces look fantastic, and the chunky geometry of the large nose, ears, and thick brow come through great. The window "eyes" are also a unique printed piece, of which this set has a surprising amount. I was pleased to find only two small sticker sheets overall. The highlight of this set is undoubtedly SpongeBob's pineapple house, though, which comes together across the remaining seven bags. The bottom floor features plenty of references to the show, including a hidden Mermaid Man and Barnacle Boy Easter egg inside the TV set, the shellphone, the photo of Gary on the wall, and even SpongeBob's "friends" Penny, Chip, and Used Napkin. Upstairs, SpongeBob's bedroom includes his bed, complete with ladder and diving board, of course, as well as his alarm clock and Gary's dessert in the corner. Don't worry, he's gonna finish it , and he's gonna like it! The designers at LEGO took a very interesting approach to recreate the rounded nature of the pineapple's exterior and its criss-crossed diamond pattern. Each one of the pinapple panels is attached to a rigid internal frame built out of Technics pieces, allowing them to sit on an angle and pivot a bit to create the rounded look. Individual panels are attached to the exterior, leaving a small gap around the edges to make the diamond pattern. While they don't fit together perfectly, the overall shape and finished house looks fantastic. Finally bringing all three houses together to recreate the Bikini Bottom landscape is a blast. Each of the bases can be connected to save space, or you can display them all freely. There's so much character to this set with endless scenes that can be recreated that it's a must-have for SpongeBob SquarePants fans. LEGO SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom, Set #11386, retails for $219.99 and is composed of 1,794 pieces. It is available to purchase exclusively from the LEGO Store . You can follow him on the site formerly known as Twitter @MatthewAdler and watch him stream on Twitch .

items.title: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023 in Pictures
items.excerpt: GTA 6 officially releases next month, so we're taking a look at how the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, have evolved since their 2023 reveal.
items.content_text: GTA 6 officially releases next month, so we're taking a look at how the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, have evolved since their 2023 reveal. If there's one thing Rockstar has consistently managed to achieve, it's that its finished games often look better than the reveal trailers. That isn't the case for many game studios. In fact, a lot of games have been slammed for being downgraded between their reveals and launches. Watch Dogs, Cyberpunk 2077, and BioShock Infinite are all solid games, but they looked even better when they were initially revealed. GTA 6 appears to have only visually improved over time, and that is most evident in the level of detail on protagonists Jason and Lucia. In 2023, we got our first official look at GTA 6 with the first trailer. There had been some leaks prior to this, but this was the first time Rockstar showed the game itself. The game looked stunning with gorgeous lighting effects, vivid colors, and realistic-looking characters. Rockstar would then go dark for a year and a half before re-revealing the game, and the graphical leap was absurdly impressive. Compared to the 2023 trailer, GTA 6's visuals have drastically changed. The overall art direction remained the same, but the level of detail presented in the character models changed massively during this period. In the first trailer, Lucia's skin looks less textured, more flat, and less nuanced. Her hair also doesn't move much; there's a bit of bounce to her ponytail, but it's more limited. She also has the same hairstyle throughout the entire trailer, outside of some loose strands of hair on the sides of her face in the opening shots. Jason only gets a few seconds to shine, but he largely looks like a generic white guy with his shaved head and stubble. Trailer 2, however, provides a lot more depth. Both characters sport a variety of hairstyles, with Lucia rocking wavy hair and a golden dress. Jason's brown hair flows out of the back of his hat. His skin glistens after sweating in the Vice City heat, his veins outline his arms, and his facial hair appears to be somewhat uneven, with certain strands of hair poking out slightly further than others. These human imperfections are perfections in the world of a video game trying to emulate realistic people. The light also bounces off of their skin in a more natural way. It's a clear showcase of not only the level of detail, but also the amount of customization the player will have. That mindset carried into the recent extended look for GTA 6. The visual leap wasn't as large as the one between trailer 1 and 2, but it does feel like a world of difference from trailer 1 itself. There's infinitely more customization options and Jason and Lucia are clearly at their final level of polish. Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson recently stated that trailer 1 was a "mission statement" for the team, as the game wasn't "fully formed." It was a north star for the team to follow and something they could point to as a way of understanding the overall vision for the game. As a result, it makes sense that the game has only improved since then. GTA 6 is just weeks away from release now and the finishing touches are being added to the game. The ESRB officially rated the game M for Mature this morning and Rockstar is starting to ramp up its marketing efforts with physical ads in places like Miami and New York. After years of waiting, GTA 6 will finally be here on November 19.

items.title: Ahead of Metro 2039, Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light Are Getting Next-Gen Updates
items.excerpt: Metro 2039 is not too far away, launching on February 4, 2027. While that game will truly bring the franchise into the current generation, developer 4A Games is launching next-gen updates for the first two games.
items.content_text: Metro 2039 is not terribly far away now, launching on February 4, 2027. While that game will truly bring the franchise to current generation consoles, developer 4A Games is launching next-gen updates for the first two games. Both Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light were incredible tech showcases for their time, but they haven't exactly aged gracefully. Despite getting an intial remaster all the way back in 2014, Metro 2033 doesn't play super well with modern hardware, and I've needed to tweak it every time I've gone back to play it. Luckily, these next-gen updates should bring some long-needed bug fixes to the game. The update will look different on console and on PC. For PS5 and Xbox Series X , the Metro games will run at either native 4K at 60 fps or an upscaled 4K at 120 fps, with PSSR on PS5 Pro and traditional temporal upscaling on the Xbox consoles. Over on PC, though, the game will finally have DLSS support, along with some unnamed quality-of-life improvements. 4A Games hasn't shared a lot of details on the updates coming to Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light, but it does promise to share full patch notes ahead of its October 22 release on PC and October 29 release on consoles. Either way, as long as the games are more stable, I'm all in. As a lifelong PC gamer, all three of the Metro games hold a special place in my heart, for all the torture they've put my graphics cards through in the past. Luckily, if you don't like putting your hardware through the wringer, it doesn't sound like 4A is going to add ray tracing or anything crazy to 2033 or Last Light, so they should be significantly easier to run at high settings than they were when they launched in 2010 and 2013. We've already gone hands-on with Metro 2039 , and it seems like an incredible and brutal post-apocalyptic shooter — just like I'd want out of the franchise. The visuals we've seen so far look incredible too, so I can only imagine that it's going to stay true to its roots of pushing PC hardware to its limits. Although, it is launching in the middle of an ongoing RAM crisis, which is going to limit its already niche appeal a bit when the benchmarks start rolling out. Here's to hoping 4A Games finds a way to make a Metro game scalable at launch for once.
